basis: Brachydactyly, joint restrictions and cardiac conduction defects define this heart-hand syndrome.
Established anthracycline-induced myocardial disease; cardiovascular damage defines the concept.
Microphthalmia, microtia and contractures define it; cardiac defects occur in 80-99%. Frequent urinary and duodenal malformations omitted under the four-axis cap.
Red-cell destruction causes anemia; the definition explicitly excludes autoimmune mediation.
Persistent patterned skin hyperpigmentation; extracutaneous abnormalities are isolated reports rather than common disease features.
Acquired metabolic fermentation localized to the bladder; yeast colonization alone does not establish invasive infection or other organ damage.
Brainstem dysfunction and deafness define it; carotid hypoplasia reported in 3/4. Central hypoventilation and supranuclear gaze palsy reflect neurologic dysfunction.
Tumor arises in a uterine supporting ligament, a reproductive structure rather than locomotor connective tissue.
Meckel syndrome features cystic renal dysplasia, encephalocele and polydactyly; hepatic ductal plate malformation/fibrosis is common, well above 30%.
LAM directly infiltrates and destroys lung tissue. Renal angiomyolipoma and TSC-associated skin lesions are distinct associated conditions.
Intestinal lymph leakage causes immunodeficiency (80-99%) and direct lymphocyte depletion (30-79%); nutritional abnormalities do not establish other organ damage.
Cardiac malformations and splenic defects define heterotaxy; asplenia 7/12. Intestinal malrotation is common; anal atresia reported in 1/2. Neural defects are uncommon.
Cerebellar degeneration with cognitive, pyramidal and sensory dysfunction; nystagmus reflects neurologic disease rather than eye damage.
Malignant neoplasm occupies the spinal cord; lymphoma is only one subtype of this cancer umbrella.
Inherited superficial acral epidermal peeling; listed hypermetropia and allergy do not establish direct extracutaneous damage from this skin disease.
Bacterial infection; no anatomical site or commonly damaged additional organ is specified.
Progressive degeneration of choroid, retinal pigment epithelium and retina; ocular vascular findings do not imply systemic vascular disease.
Broad thoracic tumor umbrella; pulmonary and pleural tumors support pulmonary assignment. Cardiac, chest-wall, neural and breast origins depend on subtype.
Intellectual disability and developmental delay define it; congenital heart abnormalities occur in 30-79%. Recurrent infections alone do not establish immunodeficiency.
Ureteral disease; ureters belong to the renal axis. Infection and neoplasia apply only to individual subtypes.
Microcornea, glaucoma and absent frontal sinuses define it; palmoplantar keratoderma occurs in 80-99%. Torus palatinus does not establish functional oral damage.
Developmental delay and speech apraxia occur in 6/6. Hypotonia is neurologic; sleep apnea in 2/6 is a separately diagnosed condition.
Inflammation of peripheral nerves in the upper limb; an autoimmune or infectious cause is not inherent to this umbrella.
Lymphoid proliferative/neoplastic umbrella dominated by lymphoma, supporting blood-cell and lymphoma mechanism axes; no common extranodal damage is specified.
Inherited susceptibility form of steatotic liver disease; hepatic steatosis is the specified phenotype, without evidence of a systemic metabolic disorder.
